entities.name: Aḥmad Ibn-Fāris
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ibn Faris was a Persian linguist, scribe, scholar, philologist and lexicographer, As well as bearing the epithet al-Rāzī, ibn Fāris was also known variously by the epithets al-Shāfiʿī, al-Mālikī, al-lughawī, al-naḥwī, al-Qazwīnī and al-Zahrāwī. He is noted for compiling two of the early dictionaries to organise words alphabetically rather than according to the word's rhyming pattern.

He was primarily associated with Ray. Initially, he was an adherent of the Shafi'i madhhab, but later switched to the Maliki. Aḥmad Ibn-Fāris was a journalists & chroniclers from Ahvaz (1000, Ahvaz–1004). Holds notable historical significance, documented across 0 language editions of Wikipedia.
